chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:

High prices and drought struck the people of Medina, to the extent that the affluent man would mix wheat with barley and eat it, and buy only part of the food (required). There was good quality food with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) which he had bought at the beginning of the year. So he said to one of his adherents: 'Buy some barley for us so I can mix it with this food, or sell it, for we dislike that we should eat good quality food while the people eat the perished (food).'
ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq demonstrate social responsibility during times of economic hardship?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructed his followers to mix their high-quality food with lower-quality grain or sell their surplus during times of scarcity and high prices. This was done to avoid the ethical issue of the wealthy eating well while the general populace suffered from poor quality or scarce food, demonstrating social solidarity and moderation in consumption. This practice, known as *khalṭ*, reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere poverty, but as a conscious choice to share in the community's hardship, ensuring that the elite do not insulate themselves from the broader societal experience of scarcity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Hammad Bin Usman who said,

‘The people of Al-Medina were hit by high prices and a drought to the extent that the affluent used to mix the wheat with the barley and he would eat it, and they would buy only part of the food (required), and there was good quality food with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> which he<sup>asws</sup> had bought it at the beginning of the year. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to one of his<sup>asws</sup> adherents: ‘Buy some barley for us<sup>asws</sup> so I<sup>asws</sup> can mix it with this food, otherwise sell it, for we<sup>asws</sup> do not like it that we<sup>asws</sup> should eat good quality food while the people eat the perished (food)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Isma’il ibn Mehran from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman who has said the following: “Once shortages of food took place in al-Madinah and even affluent people would mix wheat and barley for food and buy only a small amount of food.

Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, had a good quality of food which he had purchased earlier in the beginning of the year. He (the Imam) then asked one of his agents to buy a certain amount of barely and mix it with their good quality of food or sell this good quality of food; adding, ‘I do not like to consume good quality of food when people consume a worse quality of food.’”
